name: Todoist
tagline: Cross-platform task manager for projects, reminders, and recurring tasks

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Pro monthly changed to $7/month and $5/month annually from Dec 10, 2025.

tiers.name: Beginner
tiers.limits: 5 personal projects; 3 filters; 1 week of activity history; 5 MB files; 5 people/project.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 300 personal projects; 150 filters; 100 MB files; unlimited activity history; 5 people/project.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 300 personal projects/member; 500 team projects; 250 people/team project; 1,000 members + 1,000 guests.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 personal projects; 3 filters; 1 week of activity history; 5 MB files; 5 people/project.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Business charges per member; taxes can apply.

verdictSummary: A personal task app with projects, recurring due dates, filters, and reminders is a one-sitting/weekend build; collaboration and sync polish are the product moat.
coreLoopDIY: Create task/project tables, natural-language due date parsing, recurring rules, reminders, filters, and local notifications.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because task capture must be fast everywhere and reminders cannot miss.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Open-source task/project management app suitable as a Todoist-style alternative.

alternatives.name: Microsoft To Do
alternatives.desc: A polished free task manager, paid for with a Microsoft account rather than money

facts.install: Install the Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android app, or use the web app, and sign in with a Microsoft account
facts.dataFormat: Tasks are stored as structured records on Microsoft's Exchange Online servers and surface in Outlook Tasks across synchronized clients
facts.gapVsPaid: Microsoft To Do is weaker than Todoist on labels, custom filters, natural-language recurrence, integrations, and collaborative project workflows.

alternatives.name: Vikunja
alternatives.desc: A capable Todoist replacement once you accept becoming its hosting department

facts.install: Use the paid hosted service or deploy the free server with Docker Compose, a package, or the standalone binary
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, users, and settings live in SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, with attachments in a persistent files directory, on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Vikunja adds hosting administration and has less polished native mobile, offline, natural-language, and integration support than Todoist.
facts.setupBlocker: The free path requires a server or Docker, persistent volumes, secrets, and normally a reverse proxy with TLS

alternatives.name: Super Productivity
alternatives.desc: A local task manager with timeboxing, Pomodoro, and no account begging to be created

facts.install: Use the browser/PWA or install a packaged desktop or mobile build
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, time records, and settings are local-first in browser or app storage; optional synchronization and backups use the user's chosen WebDAV or Dropbox account
facts.gapVsPaid: Super Productivity is primarily a local personal tool and is weaker than Todoist for shared projects, mobile capture, recurring-date language, and integrations.

alternatives.name: Apple Reminders
alternatives.desc: Things minus the polish tax, provided every device in sight has an Apple logo

facts.install: Preinstalled on iPhone, iPad, and Mac; enable iCloud or another supported reminders account for synchronization
facts.engines: Optional Apple Intelligence can suggest or auto-categorize reminders on supported devices; ordinary task management does not require AI
facts.dataFormat: Structured reminder records live in iCloud or another configured reminders account and are cached on Apple devices; iCloud provides account-level restore rather than user-visible task files
facts.gapVsPaid: Apple Reminders is confined to Apple’s ecosystem and is less capable than Todoist for cross-platform collaboration, integrations, and complex filters.

notes: Strong yes; familiar product where feature creep is the real limit.
prompt:
Build me a personal task manager to replace Todoist. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered, binds to
  localhost only. Keyboard-first: n for new task, x to complete, / to search.
- Quick-add parses natural language with chrono-node: "call Sam tomorrow 4pm
  #home p2" sets due date, project, and priority in one line.
- Projects via #tags, priorities p1-p3, free-text notes on any task.
- Recurring tasks stored as rrule strings ("every 1st", "every mon,thu");
  completing one schedules the next occurrence.
- Views: Today, Upcoming (next 7 days grouped by day), and per-project. Overdue
  tasks pinned red at the top of Today.
- Reminders: node-cron checks each minute and pushes due tasks to my phone via ntfy
  (topic in .env), plus a 7am digest of today's list.
- A t add "..." CLI for capture from any terminal.
- No accounts, no telemetry, everything in one SQLite file I can back up.
- Out of scope: collaboration, native mobile apps, and offline sync. Phone access
  is ntfy notifications, that is the trade.
- README: ntfy app setup on the phone and where the DB lives.
